questions.question: What distinguishes an agent from a traditional workflow?
options: Workflows can't use AI at all
In an agent, the model decides the next step at run time
questions.explanation: In a workflow the developer fixes the steps in advance; in an agent the model chooses each step based on what it observes.

questions.question: Which task is the better fit for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?
options: Investigating why an unusual transaction was calculated a certain way
Converting a file from CSV to JSON
questions.explanation: Use an agent when you can't write down the steps in advance because each depends on what the last one found.

questions.question: What's the recommended way to introduce an agent into a business process?
options: Run it without evaluation to see what it does
Give it full write access so it can fix problems immediately
Start read-only, log every step, and add actions with approval once it's reliable
questions.explanation: Earn trust gradually: read-only first, then actions behind human approval.

questions.question: Which of these is a common agent failure mode?
options: Looping on the same failing step
questions.explanation: Agents can repeat failing steps; step limits and repetition detection help.
